newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief appoints new team but few new faces.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief appoints new team but few new faces.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan on Tuesday announced 15 senior appointments, most of whom had served in the United Nations under his predecessor, Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt.

"Change needs to be managed," said Fred Eckhard, an American who was confirmed as chief U.N. spokesman. "Rome wasn't built in a day. He will implement these changes incremently throughout this year and next year."

Among the new faces appointed by Annan, who took over as secretary-general on Jan. 1, are the heads of two key departments -- peacekeeping, which went to a Frenchman, and political affairs, which went to a Briton. Both received three-year contracts.

For undersecretary-general in charge of peacekeeping operations, Annan chose Bernard Miyet of France. His appointment is widely thought to be a reward for France, which had backed Boutros-Ghali and then lifted its veto against Annan in the Security Council election vote in December.
Miyet is France's representative to the Vienna-based Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe. Annan himself had held the post before he became secretary-general.

A British diplomat, Sir Kieran Prendergast, was named as undersecretary-general for political affairs, to succeed Marrack Goulding, also a Briton. Prendergast has served most recently as Britain's ambassador to Turkey and before that as high commissioner to Kenya. In the late 1970s he was a member of Britain's U.N. mission in New York.
